items.title: Henry A. "Hank" Kmen Interview, 1963-02-13
items.q: I used to see Larry Shields and meet him up in an apartment in the Landseer Apartments in New York that was either, I know Sharky lived in that apartment, and Johnny Beresdorfer was living in that apartment.

ctx.x: Well, specifically, getting back to what I'm supposed to be researching, I want to get some of your attitudes about early New Orleans musicians that you've heard and have some sort of impression of. You know, whether they were considered corny or good, and how you knew them and why, and just anything.

Well, at the time that I broke into the business in a professional way, generally the New Orleans musicians were, or the New Orleans style was passe. This is a time when I was kept alive by some guys who were devoted to it, you know, more or less underground. But the average working musician, at least around my area, which would be New York area, regarded that whole kind of music as corny. They called it corny. Of course, they thought of themselves as being the utmost in modernity and so forth. But then when I…
So you met the Musicians' Ball, incidentally.
